newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan gov't okays social security reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan gov't okays social security reform bill.

text.p: Venezuela's government approved Wednesday a bill to reform the country's social security system and said it would be presented to Congress immediately.

"By authorizing the presentation of this bill, a fundamental step is being taken in the development of agreements reached by the tripartite commission (of government, union and business leaders)," Information Minister Fernando Egana told reporters after a weekly cabinet meeting.

The bill will be presented in Congress Thursday by Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar, Labor Minister Maria Bernardoni, Health Minister Jose Oletta and social security reform minister Jose Miguel Uzcategui.
"The bill, which we will present tomorrow carries the unanimous and total backing of businessmen and unions," Uzcategui said.
The bill creates a framework for overhauling the social security system and would be accompanied by separate reforms to pension funds, health benefits and other aspects within the next three months.
The Inter-American Development Bank and International Labor Organization had given advice on drawing up the new bill, Uzcategui said.
Egana said the government hoped presentation of the social security reform bill would help speed up passage of a reform to Venezuela's Labor Law presented to Congress in mid-April.
The Labor Law reform is meant to replace the current system of severance payments with a new version hammered out by the tripartite commission.
